items.title: Which iPhone 18 Model Should You Buy?
items.summary: Apple's new folding iPhone Duo is finally here, alongside refreshed Pro models. Our primer has all the details you need to choose the iPhone 18 that's right for you.
items.content:
With a fresh folding form factor, the new iPhone Duo is Apple’s most radical redesign in years. It lands alongside the more familiar-looking iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. There’s no regular iPhone 18 , or at least, not yet. Rumors suggest we may see a more affordable base model, perhaps flanked by an iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air, in spring 2027.

The two new Pro iPhones are available to preorder on September 12 and ship on September 18. You can preorder the iPhone Duo from October 16, ahead of a full release on October 23. But which iPhone 18 model is right for you? I’ll break down the differences and what these phones have in common, so you can choose with confidence. For options beyond the iPhone 18 lineup, read our Best iPhones guide .

Before you drop all those hard-earned dollars, remember that you probably don’t need the latest iPhone. If you have an older iPhone, Apple does a good job of updating the software (the iPhone 11 Pro is still supported), and for hardware issues, your iPhone might be repairable ; maybe it needs a battery replacement or these troubleshooting tips . Don’t feel like you have to spring for Apple’s shiny new thing.

Sadly, Apple raised iPhone Pro prices this year, so both models are $100 more expensive than the iPhone 17 Pro series.

If you’re set on upgrading, consider raising funds by selling your old iPhone . Just be sure to back up your iPhone, and factory reset it before you sell or give it away. Once the new device arrives, we have tips on how to set up your new iPhone and what settings to change to get the most out of it.

We’ll start by looking at what’s the same across the iPhone 18 models this year.

All three new iPhones have Apple’s A20 Pro chip inside, and, you guessed it, this is Apple’s most powerful chip ever. Now, iPhones are already the most capable phones for raw compute power, but the A20 Pro promises a significant jump in performance (around 20 percent faster and 30 percent more efficient than the last generation). It also packs a new neural engine to power on-device AI and a new thermal design with a larger vapor chamber to keep things cool. For the iPhone Duo, the A20 Pro has a display engine to ensure smooth transitions between two screens. While Apple doesn’t list the RAM, every model is rumored to have 12 GB.

While they come in different sizes and the Duo has two, every iPhone features an OLED screen that Apple calls a Super Retina XDR display. They also have ProMotion technology, otherwise known as a 120-Hz refresh rate . These adaptive refresh rates can drop as low as 1 Hz when there's little activity on the screen, enabling features like the always-on display without draining the battery too much.

The displays are protected by the scratch-resistant and antireflective Ceramic Shield 2, the same as last year’s iPhone 17 range . And they can go from 1 nit up to 3,000 nits of brightness. Only the iPhone Duo has a custom nano-texture finish on the interior screen, giving it a matte look that’s designed to reduce glare and crease visibility.

All the phones have an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance, meaning they can survive a short dunk in fresh water. They all come in four storage options (256 GB, 512 GB, 1 TB, or 2 TB), support Qi2 magnetic wireless charging (MagSafe), USB-C 3.2, Dual SIM, Wi-Fi 7 , Bluetooth 6 , Thread , and Ultra-Wideband (UWB). It also has Siri AI , Apple Intelligence, Emergency SOS via Satellite, and Crash Detection.

To help you better understand which model to buy, here's precisely where they diverge.

Apple has taken its time with its first foldable, enabling it to learn from the best folding phones already on the market. Eschewing the more prevalent book- and flip-style foldables, Apple has gone with a passport-sized form factor for the iPhone Duo, similar to Samsung's recent Galaxy Z Fold8 (our current favorite). The Duo has a 5.4-inch screen on the outside, but unfolds to reveal a 7.6-inch display inside that feels like an iPad Mini.

The iPhone Duo has a tough titanium frame, a precision hinge with magnets for that satisfying snap-shut, and an IP68 rating for solid dust and water resistance. But at 254 grams and 11.3 mm thick when folded, and 5.2 mm unfolded, the Duo is not the slimmest or lightest foldable around (the Fold8 is 201 grams, 9.7 mm thick folded, and 4.5 mm unfolded).

Foldables don’t have as much space for cameras, so the Duo drops Face ID (Touch ID is in the side power button instead) and makes do without a telephoto lens (you get a 48-megapixel primary camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide). But it has room for the biggest-ever iPhone battery, promising 24 hours of mixed use.

Where Apple will likely add a lot of value to the foldable phone category is with its software design. Controls have been pushed to the side and stacked vertically to free up more screen real estate. Apps offer plenty of split-screen support, and transitions between displays look slick. Apple has also included features that take advantage of the fact that you can prop the Duo open on a table or nightstand, so there’s StandBy support to use the outer screen as an alarm clock, while the inside display gently pulses with light to wake you.

Who it’s for: You want something different. You’re curious about folding phones or already convinced they’re great and can’t wait to experience Apple’s take.

The iPhone 18 Pro is similar to last year’s 17 Pro, with a 6.3-inch display, though the Dynamic Island has been slightly slimmed and can now show three Live Activities notifications at once. It keeps the same aluminum unibody, with Ceramic Shield on the back glass, Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and an IP68 rating. Black is back, and there’s also a new Burgundy color, alongside Glacier and Silver. Those colors look more uniform than the 17 Pro’s two-tone finish.

items.title: Best Robot Lawn Mowers (2026): 12+ Models Tested Over 3 Years
items.summary: Smart mowers are an expensive alternative to old-fashioned yard work, but they’re finally good enough to consider if you’d rather sip an iced tea and watch a robot tame your lawn.
items.content:
Lawn care is a monotonous, thankless task. Who wants to mow the lawn when you could be lollygagging in a hammock with a cold drink, watching a robot do it for you? That’s right: no one. Robot lawn mowers were once the preserve of the wealthy, and yes, they can still be on the pricey side. But they’re getting cheaper and better all the time.

I’ve tested a handful of the best robot lawn mowers over the past three years , and after comparing a fresh crop this mowing season, I'm delighted to tell you that robot mowers are actually good now . I've got some recommendations, honorable mentions, and a list of robot mowers you should avoid. Read on for everything you need to know about lawn-tending bots.

Updated September 2026: I added mowers from Roborock, Segway, Eufy, and Sunseeker, added information about night mowing to the FAQ, and updated prices.

The TerraMow V1000 is a little more compact than some of the other robot mowers I’ve tested, and it comes with a covered charging station (something that often costs extra with rivals). There’s no need for wire or even an RTK antenna, because it works with a triple AI camera system, GPS, and 4G. The setup is a breeze, with impressive automatic mapping that quickly marks out your lawn in the app. You often have to remotely control mowers to map out your lawn, but I didn’t even have to edit the map, and this is the best automatic mapping I’ve seen from a robot mower.

This mower is perfect for a modest, flat rectangular lawn. It can deal with gradients up to 18 degrees, and you can set up multiple mowing zones with routes between and no-go zones. It’s surprisingly good at navigating regular paths and moving between zones. I also love the spot-mow option, which enables you to place it on any lawn and simply cut in rows using the AI vision camera (no need for mapping). Provided the lawn is fairly straightforward, it does a great, neat job. This feature is handy for front or side lawns, or even lending it to a neighbor.

Mowing performance is impressive too. The TerraMow V1000 does a neat and tidy job of mowing in lines up and down my lawn. It cut all the way to the edge where there was a path border but left the customary strip on the sides with walls, plants, and other obstacles. The obstacle avoidance is excellent, and it had no issues avoiding a football and the thin legs of a badminton net. After setting the schedule, the TerraMow V1000 finished the mow and always successfully returned to the charging station.

On the downside, the app has some messy translation and grammar, and I encountered some oddities, such as when creating my lawn map, it named it “map 3” for some reason, even after I renamed it manually. It could use a touch of polish, but functionally, I had no issues starting or stopping a mow manually. Firmware updates took a long time but completed successfully. The mower doesn’t work at night, because it relies on cameras and AI for navigation, and the front wheel isn’t great on gravel or very uneven ground. You get one year of 4G service free, and it costs $19 a year after that.

The Mammotion Luba 3 AWD can handle relatively rough terrain and steep slopes, and it combines three technologies (GPS, lidar, and AI vision) to ensure it can cut larger lawns even where there might be tree cover or other awkward spots. It’s big and heavy and requires some putting together, so it’s not the easiest to set up, but there’s no need for wire or an antenna (an RTK antenna is an optional extra for folks who lack Wi-Fi or 4G coverage in their backyard). Mammotion provides a generous three years of 4G service, and each additional year costs $50 .

This mower boasts quiet operation and efficient pathfinding. Because it’s wide, with two spinning discs underneath, you can get wide strips, and the finish is perhaps the best I’ve seen. The obstacle avoidance is solid, and it does a decent job around the edges. I also appreciate the manual mowing option, enabling you to cut any problem areas with remote app control. You can set multiple zones and tweak sensitivity for obstacles, which is handy if you’re a dog owner worried about mess. It also has a cool “drop mow” feature that lets you drop it on an unmapped area; handy if you want to loan it to a neighbor. It works well, but you can expect a bit of a border. The all-wheel drive ensures it can handle bumpy terrain and inclines. The wheel design is also great at avoiding ripping up grass, which can happen with mowers sporting big spiky wheels.

Aside from the high price, I found the wheels can get mucky and need regular cleaning. The app can also be glitchy, and occasionally connectivity drops out or takes a while. The cheapest 1500 model covers up to 0.37 acres but doesn’t include RTK. The 3000 ($2,799) covers 0.75 acres, the 5000 ($3,299) covers 1.25 acres, and both have RTK. This mower is overkill for the average yard, but it can conquer a challenging lawn.

While robot mowers are getting cheaper, they’re still expensive, so I wanted to include a budget pick in the mix. The trouble is that cheap robot mowers are still generally bad. The Anthbot M9 is as low as I would consider going right now while still being worth it. It’s currently listed at $900, but it’s frequently discounted, so don’t pay full price (I’ve seen it as low as $650). The trade-off compared to my top pick is that you still have the hassle of an RTK antenna for the GPS navigation. This model also won’t work well close to tall buildings or tree cover. The antenna needs a clear spot and it will offset the map if it gets tilted, so it must be securely in the ground (you do get a warning in the app about this if it tilts).

items.title: Google is making it easier to switch between password managers on Android
items.summary: Google's new feature will transfer your passkeys as well.
items.content:
Google on Thursday introduced a new password manager switching experience on Android that doesn’t require you to download CSV files when migrating to a new app.

With the new feature, users will be able to move all of their passwords — and even passkeys — between apps seamlessly.

To use the new system, users first open their new password manager app and choose to import or copy passwords from the old manager app. Android will detect manager apps on the device and coordinate transfer between both apps. Users can review the information being transferred and approve it in a few taps.

Because this method also supports passkey transfer, users won’t need to set them up again when moving to a new password manager app. Plus, the company said that this averts the risk of exposing data from a CSV file.

Google said the new experience is already available on select partners as well as in Google’s own password manager app. Bitwarden, 1Password, and Dashlane are currently supported, with more apps coming in the future.

The password manager switching feature will be available on all devices running Android 8 or above.

items.title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
items.summary: A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas - before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized. Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration's Advanced Air Mobility a
items.content:
The flights will be conducted under the White House’s new pilot program to test out electric, hybrid, and autonomous aircraft.

A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas — before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized.

Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration’s Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) selected eight state-led projects to serve as some of the first public tests of these new aircraft. The first one kicks off today in Texas, featuring three eVTOL companies: Joby, Beta, and Wisk.

For the next week, these companies will conduct test flights demonstrating future routes between cities and regional airports, including Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. The aircraft won’t carry any passengers, but regulators will be keen to see how the state’s air traffic control system handles the uptick in flight traffic. The companies, meanwhile, are eager to prove to the federal government that their aircraft deserve to be awarded type certification, which is required before any of them can carry passengers commercially in the US.

But type certification can take years to attain, which led to the White House to create this pilot program allowing these companies to demonstrate their new technology — even before the regulatory process has concluded. Through the eIPP, the companies hope to accelerate their path to market by getting a head start on data collection that will be needed for certification. Data from the program will also be used to “develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale,” the White House said earlier.

The companies say they are thrilled to demonstrate the future of electric and autonomous flight, which they argue will help reduce car traffic in cities and open up new mobility opportunities for consumers.

“I’m incredibly excited by the potential for vertical lift in Texas, a state with the infrastructure, expertise, and partnerships to help lead the next era of American aviation,” JoeBen Bevirt, Founder and CEO of Joby Aviation, said in a statement.

Several of these companies have conducted public test flights before — Joby’s egg-shaped aircraft demonstrated its future route between Lower Manhattan and JFK Airprot earlier this year — but these will be the first official flights under the White House’s new pilot program. Additional tests are being planned in New York, Utah, Pennsylvania, Louisiana, Florida, North Carolina, and New Mexico.

Legal in-fighting , however, could muddy the picture for electric aviation. Joby and one of its rivals, Archer, are currently suing each other for stolen trade secrets and corporate espionage. Technology limitations, including battery weight and sensor decisions, could also hamper the rollout.

items.title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
items.summary: Universal Music Group is launching a new AI-powered platform that will allow users to draw from its catalog of licensed music to create song remixes, mashups, and new takes on tracks, according to an announcement on Thursday. The record label is developing the platform through a
items.content:
UMG’s AI music platform will let users create remixes, mashups, and new takes on tracks.

Universal Music Group is launching a new AI-powered platform that will allow users to draw from its catalog of licensed music to create song remixes, mashups, and new takes on tracks, according to an announcement on Thursday . The record label is developing the platform through a multiyear licensing agreement with ElevenLabs, a company that specializes in AI voice and music generation.

Artists can choose whether to participate in UMG and ElevenLabs’ upcoming platform, which marks yet another AI deal for the record label. UMG is currently developing an AI music platform with Udio and has struck AI licensing deals with Spotify , Nvidia , and Klay . This week, Suno released its first AI music model trained on licensed songs from Warner Music Group, BMG, and music industry partners.

UMG and ElevenLabs’ partnership will also include the “development of additional products and fan experiences in the months and years to come,” though the press release doesn’t include other details about what this might entail.

”By combining UMG’s global community and rights management expertise, with our AI models and products, we’ll enable artists and songwriters to create powerful new experiences for their fans, and ensure they are fairly compensated,” ElevenLabs CEO Mati Staniszewski says in the press release. The new AI music platform will remain separate from ElevenLabs’ Music API and ElevenMusic generator .

items.title: Where to preorder the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
items.summary: The iPhone Duo was the unequivocal star of Apple's "Surprise and shine" event, but not for people who were mostly paying attention for news on wearables. Thankfully, Apple had a lot to share about its new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. There's no update to the SE model for 20
items.content:
Longer battery life and a more capable chipset (that enables a host of new features) are the main reasons to upgrade.

If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The iPhone Duo was the unequivocal star of Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event , but not for people who were mostly paying attention for news on wearables. Thankfully, Apple had a lot to share about its new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 . There’s no update to the SE model for 2026, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing ( the SE 3 rules ). Also, no price changes either, which can’t be said for the entire iPhone lineup .

While both new watches look similar to their predecessors, there are a number of updates under the hood that might intrigue some people enough to warrant a preorder. My colleague Victoria Song got hands-on with both smartwatches , and runs down the biggest changes, from the Audio Intelligence features made possible by the S11 chip (included in the Series 12 and Ultra 4), plus the possible impact of its improved sensors and tracking capabilities.

If you don’t want to wait for reviews to hit before you make the purchase, the Series 12 starts at $399 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Apple itself for the 42mm size ($50 more for the 46mm). High rollers can configure one with a ceramic case (the first time ceramic has been on the menu since the Series 5) starting at $899. Like usual, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799 from Amazon and Best Buy and comes in one size, which features GPS and 5G support. Launches will occur on September 18th, the same day as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

items.title: Wolverine on the PS5 goes back to a simpler (and bloodier) style of action game
items.summary: Marvel's Wolverine captures just how angry its lead character is. The latest PS5 exclusive from Spider-Man developer Insomniac, Wolverine is a straightforward action game that is at its best when you're (literally) slicing through enemies or thrust into a sequence pulled from a b
items.content:
The next few months are packed with new games, and PlayStation goes old-school to cut through the noise.

Marvel’s Wolverine captures just how angry its lead character is. The latest PS5 exclusive from Spider-Man developer Insomniac , Wolverine is a straightforward action game that is at its best when you’re (literally) slicing through enemies or thrust into a sequence pulled from a blockbuster movie, like climbing the fuselage of a plane as it careens toward land or racing a motorcycle across rain-slicked city streets. It’s the kind of game that can really get your heart rate rising, and keeping Logan mad is a key part of the strategy. In many ways, it’s a throwback to straightforward action titles of the past — and it’s a refreshing change of pace in a medium saturated with live-service and open-world games.

Though it comes from Insomniac, Wolverine is very different from Spider-Man , which thrust the web-slinger into an open-world version of New York City. Instead, this is a much more linear experience that feels like a combination of two other PlayStation staples: God of War and Uncharted . Rather than follow Wolverine as a member of the X-Men, the story instead has him as an often reluctant member of Team X, a mercenary group with similar pro-mutant aims but a much more violent approach. Instead of heroes like Cyclops and Professor X, Wolvy is joined by more villain-adjacent characters like Sabretooth, Mystique, and Nathaniel Essex, before eventually connecting with Jean Grey. The story pulls Logan and his companions across the globe, but it starts out relatively simple, as they investigate a rash of mutant disappearances connected to a billionaire arms dealer.

The most important thing about both Wolverine the character and Wolverine the game is fighting. This is a hairy little dude who loves to scrap, and his mutant powers — healing and sharp claws — make it so that he is very good at it, able to both take a huge amount of damage and dish it out. And the best part of the game is how Wolverine-specific the action is. The combat is fast and violent and forces you to be aggressive. Wolverine can leap huge distances to take out foes and use his claws to both repel attacks and slice at enemies, often with very gruesome results. (At the end of a battle he’s usually coated in blood.) An important part of this is Wolverine’s rage level, which increases the more you fight. As his rage grows, it allows you to do two things: go absolutely berserk and kill a rash of enemies with a single blow, and use your healing power as a sort of extra life in case your health depletes. It’s a clever system that means you can’t sit back and play it safe. Wolverine isn’t chill, and you can’t be either.

That’s the God of War side of Wolverine . The Uncharted side comes in the form of all of the over-the-top set-pieces you’re thrown into. I’ll refrain from detailing some of the best ones for spoiler reasons, but I’ll say that, just like in Uncharted , these moments make it feel like you’re playing out a wild sequence from an action movie. There are chases across the rooftops of Tokyo, massive boss battles against some iconic comic book villains, and scenes where Wolverine is literally being ripped apart as he fights for survival.

The flip side is that, because of this setup, Wolverine is also much more restrictive than most of its contemporaries. In some ways this is a good thing; it’s refreshing to play a game that isn’t trying to do everything . But there are still some awkward elements. For instance, much like in Spider-Man , there are lots of collectibles that will reveal new bits of story or unlock new suits for Wolverine to wear. But exploration outside of the main path is extremely dull, so the only reason to track these down is if you have a completionist mindset. It’s also disappointing that Wolverine’s closet of outfits is much less fun than Spider-Man’s , and they often feel out of place with the game’s attempt at a more gritty tone.

Making matters worse is that, despite a promising start, the story ends up in a largely forgettable place, with few surprises, particularly if you have an even slight knowledge of the X-Men universe from comics or the animated series. Outside of combat and set-pieces, Wolverine skews generic AAA game; the voice acting, the cutscenes, and even some of the missions feel like standard video game fare, many of which seem out of place. Wolverine is amazing when you’re surrounded by ninjas trying to kill you. But when Logan is in a tux trying to spy on a fancy party? Not so much.

All that said, Wolverine ’s return to a simpler and smaller style of action — I beat the game in around 13 hours — is still notable, particularly from Sony, which has had a rough few years after placing many ill-fated bets in the live-service space . But much like last year’s Ghost of Yōtei , Wolverine shows that PlayStation is still capable of the single-player blockbusters the platform is best known for. It’s also launching at perhaps the busiest video game release period in recent memory, going up against major titles including Onimusha: Way of the Sword , Control Resonant , Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave , Gears of War: E-Day , Silent Hill: Townfall , Star Wars: Zero Company , and, soon enough, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Grand Theft Auto VI .

In that company, despite occasionally skewing generic, Wolverine ’s bloodthirsty focus on action is something that makes it stand out.

Marvel’s Wolverine launches on September 15th on the PS5 .

items.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
items.summary: Meta has launched its new Muse assistant, marking the company's first real foray into AI-powered productivity tools. The company says its AI agent can "take the busywork off your plate" by helping you with online shopping, emails, trip-planning, and more. I decided to try out the
items.content:
Muse rattled off very specific interests linked to my Instagram account.

Meta has launched its new Muse assistant, marking the company’s first real foray into AI-powered productivity tools. The company says its AI agent can “take the busywork off your plate” by helping you with online shopping , emails, trip-planning, and more. I decided to try out the new tool and see how well it performed — especially from a company that previously prioritized entertainment over productivity. Though the AI assistant generally worked as I expected it to, the unnerving amount of information it autonomously gleaned about me largely overshadowed my experience.

One of the first tasks I assigned Muse, which carries out actions using a cloud-based virtual computer, was to sort through my Gmail inbox and delete messages I don’t need. That required me to connect Muse to my Google account and give it permission to access, read, and delete emails. The process didn’t go smoothly on mobile; the Google sign-in screen kept glitching and returning me to the Muse website instead of the app. I eventually got it working on my laptop, where it deleted thousands of promotional emails and updates. I didn’t feel good about permitting Muse to view all of my emails given Meta’s track record on privacy over the years.

Meta says it designed Muse to only exchange data with third-party apps “that’s needed for them to work for you.” The company also says that it doesn’t share your information with advertisers. I still felt uneasy, but I pushed on anyway, linking my Amazon account to Muse. I asked the AI agent to pick out workout tops for me based on a specific size, style, and colors. Before placing the order, Muse noticed I had other items in my cart and asked if I wanted to remove them. The consideration pleasantly surprised me. Once I signed off on the purchase, it proceeded to successfully buy only the tank tops.

Shifting gears, I tried out some of Muse’s other capabilities, which allow it to generate AI podcasts similar to Gemini Notebook, create images and videos, as well as develop interactive webpages or documents called “artifacts.” Muse denied my requests to generate images of a “cartoon mouse with red pants” and a “cartoon guy with a red hat, blue overalls, brown hair, and a mustache.

However, it readily generated a video and several images of a product launch event featuring devices with Apple’s logo when asked. In one image, Muse created what looks like an iPhone-like foldable, an Apple Watch, and AirPods. Each device is propped up on a stand with Apple’s logo on it, while a presenter stands in front of a backdrop plastered with the company’s recognizable bitten apple. The phone even included Apple’s native app icons on the fake iPhone, though it hallucinated and named the App Store “Photos,” while calling Maps, Music, and the actual Photos app “Calender.” Muse refused to generate an image of an “Apple CEO.”

Then things got weird. I tapped over to the “Feed” tab, where Muse generates a news feed of sorts based on a text prompt. I submitted the prompt that Meta includes by default: “Make me a feed about my interests. Keep the tone clear and direct. Ensure it is quick to skim. Try to avoid clickbait.” It returned several AI-generated summaries of current events, including blurbs about Apple’s iPhone Duo launch event, the dangerous surf hitting California’s coast, and tankers destroyed in the Iran war. The app also listed several news stories from the state where I’m currently visiting my family, which Muse admitted it pulled from the shipping address on my Amazon order.

I dove deeper from there and asked Muse what else it might know about me based on the Instagram and Facebook accounts I signed up to use the AI agent with. It rattled off my very specific interests, ranging from anime and CrossFit to Labrador retrievers, Florida wildlife, and ’90s/2000s nostalgia — many of the same topics that frequently pop up in my Instagram Reels feed.

Curious, I asked Muse to tell me where it got that information. “Honestly, Instagram doesn’t show you that exact list anywhere in the app — I read it through the account’s API data, which surfaces more than the UI does,” Muse wrote. “The closest thing you can see yourself is your ad topics… That shows the topics advertisers can target you with, and you can remove ones you don’t want or choose to see less of them.” I checked the “Ad topics” list in my Instagram settings menu, and while it does include some vague categories, like workouts, music, and electronics, it’s not the same level of detail that Muse provided. The Verge reached out to Meta about the data Muse can access inside Instagram and Facebook but didn’t immediately hear back.

Like some of the other agentic AI tools I’ve tried out, Muse does a decent job at performing low-stakes tasks. I also like that it generates a running list of “ideas” that give personalized suggestions on how to use the tool, like providing side-by-side comparisons of products, finding and cancelling forgotten subscriptions, and keeping track of the next release of Pokémon cards. Muse keeps a running list of “goals” to complete based on your conversations with the AI agent, too.

Muse delivered on its promise of handling life’s more mundane tasks in the background, but the level of personal details Muse scooped up from sources unavailable even to me was enough to leave me with an uneasy feeling about letting Muse sort through personal emails and handle my credit card. That level of suspicion is going to be the real hurdle for Meta to overcome.
